title: Pepper pot soup

{{Short description|Tripe soup}} {{Use mdy dates|date=December 2023}} {{Infobox food | name = Philadelphia pepper pot | image = John Lewis Krimmel - A Scene in the Philadelphia Market (1811).jpg | caption = ''[[Pepper-Pot: A Scene in the Philadelphia Market]]'' (1811) by [[John Lewis Krimmel]]
The scene depicts a pepper pot soup street vendor in Philadelphia serving soup from a pot to customers.{{cite web | title = Africans in America - Part 3: 1791-1831 | work = Historical Documents - Pepper-Pot: A Scene in the Philadelphia Market - 1811 | publisher = [[WGBH-TV|WGBH]] | date = | url = https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/aia/part3/3h251.html | accessdate = 2008-01-17 }} | alternate_name = | country = United States | region = Philadelphia | course = | type = [[Soup]]/ [[Stew]] | served = | main_ingredient = Beef [[tripe]], [[vegetable]]s, pepper, other [[seasoning]]s | variations = | calories = | other = }} '''Pepper pot soup''' is a thick [[stew]] of beef [[tripe]], vegetables, pepper and other seasonings. The soup was first made in South America and the Caribbean before being brought to North America through slave trade and made into a distinctively Philadelphian dish by colonial Black women during the nineteenth century. It was one of the first street foods in the United States, sold by so-called "Pepper Pot women", and was at one point the symbolic food of the city of [[Philadelphia]].{{Cite web|date=2019-09-04|title=Pepper Pot Soup Recipe: How to Make the Historic Philadelphia Staple|url=https://thephiladelphiacitizen.org/pepper-pot-soup-recipe/|access-date=2021-09-21|website=The Philadelphia Citizen|language=en-US}}
